name: Screen and diligence private equity co-investments
summary: General partners in the organisation's private equity funds offer it stakes in individual buyouts alongside the fund, usually with no management fee or carried interest but with a deadline of three to six weeks. A small team of associates and principals screens each offer against the private equity plan, reads the sponsor's diligence reports, rebuilds the returns model, adds its own expert calls and an ESG review, and writes a memo that the managing director, the independent risk team and the investment committee must clear before the deadline. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for the sponsor's answers, reviewers and committee slots, and many deals are lost after the work is done because the sponsor loses the auction or the team declines.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial public-sector asset manager of about 240 staff with a nine-person private equity team building a co-investment programme beside its fund commitments.
baseline.notes: Private equity holdings were segregated client holdings in the period, so each approved ticket is split across client portfolios. Investment committee and independent risk review are separate processes in the organisation file; this workflow models only the deal team's work and waits for them.

unit_of_work: one co-investment taken into due diligence
trigger: A general partner offers a co-investment and the team signs a confidentiality agreement to look at it.
end_state: The deal is approved by the investment committee and handed to legal for closing, or it is declined or lost with the sponsor told and the file closed.

volume.seasonality: Follows sponsor deal flow: busier in the second and fourth quarters and in 2021, quieter in the spring of 2020.

evidence.note: Eight new co-investments or direct deals and two follow-ons in 2021; with about a quarter of deeply investigated deals closing, about 36 a year enter diligence.
Duties from the model manager posting; FTE from simulated hands-on time; cost from the organisation file.

Approves pursuit, signs off memos and presents to committee; FTE from simulated hands-on time.

systems.name: Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Document management system and virtual data rooms
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)

steps.name: Log the co-investment offer and request the NDA
steps.description: A general partner emails a co-investment teaser with a response deadline and its confidentiality agreement. The associate records the company, sponsor, ticket size, structure (syndication after signing or co-underwriting before signing) and deadline in the pipeline tracker and sends the agreement to legal.

evidence.note: GPs extend offers at their discretion with short deadlines; tracker fields are the author's choice.

steps.name: Review and sign the confidentiality agreement
steps.description: Investment counsel compares the agreement with the organisation's standard positions: affiliates and clients covered, permission to share with advisers and financing sources, non-solicitation and term. Counsel marks up unacceptable clauses, agrees changes with the sponsor's lawyers and signs under delegated authority.

error.defect_description: A broad non-solicitation or standstill clause is accepted that later restricts other teams.

control.basis: Legal review and signing authority for confidentiality agreements under the delegation of authority

next.condition: sponsor rejects the mark-up; another round

evidence.note: Access to confidential information depends on an agreement that allows sharing; the 15% second-round share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Add the company to the watch list
steps.description: The compliance analyst adds the target and, where relevant, its listed debt or equity and the sponsor's public vehicles to the watch or restricted list in the pre-trade compliance engine. This stops public market teams trading on information from the data room and records who is over the wall.

control.basis: Ontario Securities Act section 76 (trading or tipping with undisclosed material facts); internal information barrier and restricted list procedure

evidence.note: Common practice at asset owners with internal public market teams; no source opened on this organisation's procedure.

steps.name: Run the first screen in the data room
steps.description: The associate opens the virtual data room, reads the sponsor's investment memo and management materials and checks fit with the annual private equity plan: sector, region, ticket size, concentration and room in each client's allocation. The associate checks the sponsor's co-investment record and strike zone and runs a quick returns check on the sponsor's model. The time includes a share of the desk screening of the two or so offers turned down at first look for every one taken into diligence.

error.defect_description: Concentration or client allocation room is misread, so a deal goes forward that cannot be sized.

evidence.note: Sponsor co-investment policy and record as in ILPA DDQ section 5; strike zone and track record checks from Cambridge Associates; first-look share from the deal funnel (fewer than 24 of 100 opportunities get deep diligence).

steps.name: Decide whether to pursue and write a screening note
steps.description: The principal goes through the screen with the associate, decides whether the deal merits full work and writes a short note to the managing director with the thesis, main risks, workplan, proposed adviser spend and the sponsor's deadline.

evidence.note: Selective screening against a 'do every deal' approach; the 25% early drop is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve full diligence and adviser budget
steps.description: The managing director reads the note, usually at the weekly team meeting, confirms fit with the plan and relationship with the sponsor and approves time and outside adviser spend. Deals the managing director does not support are declined here.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for pursuit decisions and external adviser spend

evidence.note: The managing director leads evaluation of co-investments; the approval gate and 10% rejection are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Attend the sponsor deal team call and management presentation
steps.description: The associate prepares questions, then joins the sponsor's deal team call and the management presentation with the principal, covering the investment thesis, value creation plan, financing, exit routes and how the sponsor sized the co-investment tranche.

evidence.note: LPs usually speak with the deal team; GPs should explain why a co-investment tranche is offered.

steps.name: Review the sponsor's diligence reports
steps.description: The associate signs the advisers' non-reliance letters and reads the quality of earnings, commercial, legal, tax, insurance and environmental reports the sponsor commissioned, noting gaps, aggressive adjustments and questions for the sponsor.

error.defect_description: An earnings adjustment or legal finding in a sponsor report is missed.

evidence.note: Advisers commonly require non-reliance letters; co-investors must question reports commissioned by the GP.

steps.name: Send follow-up questions to the sponsor
steps.description: The associate consolidates open points from the reports, the call and the model into a question list, agrees it with the principal and sends it to the sponsor's deal team with a requested reply date.

evidence.note: LPs want more time and data; question round is common practice.

steps.name: Wait for the sponsor's answers
steps.description: The sponsor's deal team answers questions, adds documents to the data room and sometimes arranges an expert or management follow-up call. Co-investors compete with lenders and other co-investors for the sponsor's attention.

evidence.note: Two to seven days for a question round, set so the whole process fits the four to six week window.

steps.name: Rebuild and stress-test the returns model
steps.description: The associate rebuilds the sponsor's operating and financing case in the team's template, adds downside and exit-multiple cases, foreign exchange and fees, and computes IRR and multiple for the organisation's ticket and for each client's share.

error.defect_description: Formula, currency or share count error changes the returns shown.

evidence.note: Associates build complex financial models; co-investors stress-test the GP's model.

steps.name: Review ESG risks and the sponsor's ESG work
steps.description: The responsible investing analyst applies the organisation's ESG framework and sector standards, reads the sponsor's ESG diligence, screens news and controversy databases and estimates climate exposure, then writes the ESG section and any conditions for the memo.

control.basis: Responsible investing policy: ESG assessment required in due diligence for direct and co-investments

evidence.note: The model manager uses an ESG framework with sector-specific standards to assess direct investments in due diligence.

steps.name: Run own diligence on the key risks
steps.description: The principal calls industry experts, references on management and the sponsor's operating partner, compares the entry price with listed and deal comparables and decides whether an own adviser is needed for a specific risk such as tax structure or a key customer.

evidence.note: Underwrite the deal team and deal merits; the 25% own-adviser share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for an outside adviser's confirmatory work
steps.description: An accounting, tax or industry adviser engaged for the co-investor does a narrow confirmatory review and reports back, usually within one to three weeks and against the sponsor's deadline.

evidence.note: One to three weeks, bounded by the four to six week syndication window.

steps.name: Decide whether to take the deal to committee
steps.description: The principal and associate go through the model, ESG view and risk findings and decide whether to write a memo, ask the sponsor more questions or decline. Some deals stop because the sponsor loses the auction or fills the tranche elsewhere.

next.condition: sponsor loses the deal or fills the tranche

evidence.note: About a quarter of deeply investigated deals close; co-underwriting carries no certainty the GP wins. Branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the investment memo
steps.description: The associate writes the committee memo: thesis, sponsor and co-investment record, business and market, valuation and financing, returns and downside cases, key risks and mitigants, ESG, fees and terms, proposed size and split across client portfolios.

error.defect_description: Numbers in the memo do not match the model or a risk is left out.

evidence.note: Associates prepare investment committee materials.

steps.name: Review and revise the memo
steps.description: The principal checks the memo against the model and diligence findings, sharpens the recommendation and sends comments back to the associate or forwards the memo to the managing director.

evidence.note: Two-level review before committee is common practice; 25% return rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Managing director signs off the memo
steps.description: The managing director reads the memo, tests the sizing and fit with the private equity plan and either signs off for committee or asks for changes.

control.basis: Investment approval policy: asset class head sponsors every committee submission

evidence.note: The managing director prepares and presents deals to the investment committee.

steps.name: Submit the memo to risk and the committee secretariat
steps.description: The associate files the memo, model, ESG assessment and conflict declarations in the committee portal and sends them to the investment risk team for its independent opinion, asking for a committee slot before the sponsor's deadline.

evidence.note: Submission mechanics are the author's estimate; the risk opinion and committee are separate processes in the organisation file.

steps.name: Answer the independent risk review
steps.description: While the investment risk team writes its opinion, the principal answers its questions on leverage, concentration, currency, liquidity and valuation, and agrees any changes to the memo.

control.basis: Investment risk policy: an independent risk opinion accompanies every investment committee paper

next.condition: risk issue needs a memo change

evidence.note: The organisation file routes every memo to new-investment-risk-review; timing and rework share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Present the deal at the investment committee
steps.description: The managing director and principal present the memo at the next weekly or a special committee meeting chaired by the chief investment officer, answer questions and receive the decision: approve, approve with conditions, defer for more work or decline.

control.basis: Board-approved investment approval authorities: investment committee approval of direct and co-investments within delegated limits

evidence.note: Deals are presented to the investment committee; outcome shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the commitment and allocation with the sponsor
steps.description: The principal tells the sponsor the approved amount and any conditions, confirms the vehicle and closing timetable and asks for the final allocation.

evidence.note: LPs give a size range and the GP allocates when demand exceeds supply.

steps.name: Wait for the sponsor's final allocation
steps.description: The sponsor collects indications from all co-investors, signs or completes the acquisition and confirms each allocation, which may be cut back. A few deals fall away because the sponsor loses or abandons the transaction.

next.condition: sponsor loses or abandons the deal

evidence.note: Allocation by the GP; pre-signing offers risk the GP not winning. Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the legal instruction and hand over to closing
steps.description: The principal sends legal the term sheet, approved amount, conditions, client split and vehicle documents to review, copies private markets operations for funding, and updates the pipeline tracker.

evidence.note: Co-investor rights in the vehicle need counsel review; legal negotiation is the separate investment-legal-agreements process.

steps.name: Tell the sponsor and close the file
steps.description: The associate tells the sponsor the organisation will not participate, keeping the relationship warm, records the reason in the pipeline tracker and asks compliance to lift the watch list entry when appropriate.

evidence.note: Common practice; the time is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Sponsor loses the auction or fills the tranche
exceptions.description: In co-underwriting the sponsor has not yet won the company; when it loses, or fills the tranche with other co-investors, all diligence work is written off.

exceptions.name: Second confidentiality round
exceptions.description: The sponsor's lawyers reject the mark-up and the agreement goes round again, delaying data room access by a few days.

exceptions.name: Own adviser engaged
exceptions.description: A specific risk needs the organisation's own accountant, tax adviser or industry consultant, adding one to three weeks.

exceptions.name: Committee defers or risk team objects
exceptions.description: The risk opinion or the committee asks for more analysis, sending the memo back for a rewrite against the sponsor's deadline.

exceptions.name: Allocation cut back
exceptions.description: The tranche is oversubscribed and the sponsor allocates less than approved; the client split is redone before legal instruction.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from offer to binding commitment
benchmarks.population: Private equity co-investment syndications offered to limited partners

evidence.note: Four to six weeks from first contact to binding agreement for a syndication, three to four weeks for co-underwriting; p90 is the author's estimate.

benchmarks.unit: share of deals deeply investigated that close

evidence.note: Fewer than 24 of 100 opportunities deeply investigated and 6 closed.
Eight new co-investments or direct deals and two follow-on investments.

pain_points.description: Sponsor deadlines of three to six weeks collide with a chain of internal sign-offs (managing director, independent risk, investment committee), so memos are written in a rush and committee slots are a bottleneck.

evidence.note: Short windows and the need to evaluate quickly.

pain_points.description: The team relies on reports the sponsor commissioned, under non-reliance letters, and has little time to commission its own work.
Model and memo work sits with one associate per deal, so two live deals at once stretch the team and errors between model and memo are found late.

evidence.note: Team of four associates for about 36 diligence cases a year plus fund work.

pain_points.description: A large share of diligence ends with no investment because the sponsor loses the deal, the tranche is filled or the team declines, so much effort is written off.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Private equity: eight new co-investments or direct deals and two follow-on investments in 2021, four new fund partners committing $1.47 billion, two co-investments alongside Ardian and one alongside GI Partners; an ESG framework with sector-specific standards is used to assess fund managers and direct investments in due diligence. Infrastructure: over $3 billion of transactions in 2021, first control acquisition (100% of Pulse Clean Energy), about 10% of AusNet Services in a take-private alongside Brookfield and Canadian peers, direct investing alongside funds or strategic partners. Real estate: $225 million committed to 12 industrial development projects with WPT REIT, a multi-family joint venture, first life sciences co-investment, four properties sold. First Client Forum and an evolved client relationship management framework.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: 200 fund managers (including underlying funds) in mid-2019, 124 at end 2020 and a plan for about 80 to 85 by mid-2021; fund-of-funds eliminated; one-time manager transition costs in 2020 from repositioning public equity portfolios; hedge fund portfolio moved from fund-of-funds to direct hedge fund investments on a managed account platform; senior roles filled to support more direct and co-investing; a client engagement protocol rolled out to all employees in December 2020 setting guidelines and accountability for client communications.

sources.title: Six Things to Know About Co-investments
sources.supports: A typical syndication lasts four to six weeks from first contact to binding agreement; in co-underwriting, LPs must commit in three to four weeks with no certainty the GP wins; LPs usually pay no management fee or carry; diligence should test the GP's co-investment track record, the deal's fit with the GP's strike zone, the deal team and deal merits, and require adequate materials and quarterly reporting; a typical co-investment is about 25% of a fund commitment; large programmes are limited mainly by time and resources to evaluate deals.

sources.title: Private Equity Co-Investments: The Full Guide
sources.supports: LP side of a co-investment: GP extends the offer at its discretion, sends diligence materials, market research and its financial model; LPs review and do their own diligence over several weeks, stress-test the GP's materials and question consultant reports the GP commissioned; LPs give a size range and the GP allocates when oversubscribed; GPs want indications within days or weeks; most co-investments are fee-free and carry-free; pre-closing offers carry the risk that the GP does not win the deal.

sources.title: Private Equity Co-Investments (Pepper Hamilton LLP, J. Corelli and P. T. Le)
sources.supports: Co-investors must evaluate opportunities quickly; access to confidential information is fundamental and confidentiality agreements must allow sharing; sponsors may share diligence reports but advisers often require a non-reliance letter; deal documents are often take-it-or-leave-it; co-investor rights in the vehicle (pre-emptive, tag-along, information rights) need counsel review; each co-investor bears its own review costs.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0
sources.supports: Co-investment allocation: GPs should disclose an allocation framework, give prospective co-investors the reason for offering a co-investment tranche, disclose differentiated economics and allocate broken deal and co-investment expenses consistently; GPs may pre-qualify LPs' interest and ability to execute co-investments.

sources.title: ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0
sources.supports: Section 5 on co-investments: the fund's co-investment policy and allocation, past co-investments, transaction fees, management fees and carry charged to co-investors, syndicated versus pre-signing co-underwriting deals, governance rights offered and treatment of broken-deal expenses.

sources.title: What Do Private Equity Firms Say They Do? (NBER Working Paper 21133)
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Economic Research (P. Gompers, S. Kaplan, V. Mukharlyamov)
sources.supports: Survey of 79 PE firms: for every 100 opportunities considered, the average firm deeply investigates fewer than 24, signs fewer than 14 and closes 6; firms devote considerable resources to deals they do not do; about a third of closed deals come from investment bank auctions.

sources.title: Senior Analyst / Associate, Private Equity (The model manager job posting)
sources.publisher: Canadian Venture Capital and Private Equity Association job board
sources.supports: The model manager associate duties: assist the private equity team in due diligence for its funds and co-investments programme, build complex financial models and valuation analyses, prepare reports and presentation materials for investment committees; 1 to 5 years of private markets or banking experience.

sources.title: Managing Director, Private Equity (Co-Investments) (The model manager job posting)
sources.supports: The model manager managing director leads sourcing, evaluation and execution of co-investments, secondaries and fund commitments; oversees due diligence (industry and company analysis, financial modelling, legal negotiations); prepares and presents deals to the investment committee; builds relationships with general partners.

assumptions: The case starts when the team signs a confidentiality agreement; offers declined at first look without one are not cases, but their screening time is folded into the first screen step.
Investment committee decisions and independent risk opinions are separate processes; this workflow carries the deal team's time and the waits for those processes only.
About 29% of cases end approved, consistent with ten private equity co-investments, direct deals and follow-ons in 2021 from about 36 diligence cases.
The watch list step is modelled for every case although it matters most for listed targets or issuers with public debt.
Waits include the elapsed spread of multi-day tasks, because the simulator adds hands-on minutes as elapsed time without working-day calendars.

The cycle time benchmark covers completed syndications; the simulated median over all cases is shorter because many cases are declined within the first two weeks. Approved cases take about six weeks in the simulation.
Roles, titles and hourly costs come from the organisation file; full-time equivalents are set from simulated hands-on time times volume, within the headcount left after other workflows.
